profiles.meeting_scenario: A planning meeting for a 3-week internal replication-and-extension study based on the paper topic "Deep Learning: A Bayesian Perspective," using Airbnb booking prediction as the anchor application. The context is that the lab wants a workshop submission that revisits the Bayesian framing of deep learning on the Airbnb task and adds a short modern commentary on uncertainty estimation. The agenda is to decide what counts as the initial replication, which dataset and lab assets to use, who owns experiments versus writing, and what intermediate milestones should be hit next week. The expected outcome is a concrete task split, a shared timeline for experiments and drafting, and agreement on what the first checkpoint should deliver.

members.name: Dr. Lena Moravec
members.expertise: Bayesian deep learning, approximate inference, statistical learning theory
members.background: An associate professor who has published on Bayesian interpretations of optimization and regularization, and who typically shapes the framing and claims of workshop papers while delegating experimental execution.
members.private_state: She wants a credible, fast-moving replication that can support a workshop submission and later feed into a grant narrative, and she is wary of the project expanding into a large engineering benchmark before there is a coherent story.
hidden_assumptions: When someone says "the Airbnb data," they mean the archived Kaggle New User Bookings dataset snapshot the lab has used for prior reproductions.
A "replication" should stay close to the original paper's preprocessing and evaluation setup unless the team explicitly decides on deviations later.
The "standard split" is the fixed train/validation partition stored in the old lab reproduction repository for this task.
Results are "draft-ready" once there is one stable comparison table and enough uncertainty estimates to support the narrative, even if the run matrix is not fully exhausted.

members.name: Kai Deshpande
members.expertise: Experiment pipelines, reproducible ML systems, large-scale model training and evaluation
members.background: A senior research engineer with prior recommender-systems experience who usually converts research ideas into standardized pipelines, tracked experiments, and reusable artifacts for the lab.
members.private_state: He wants the project to fit the lab's current reproducibility standards and avoid one-off scripts, and he is concerned that informal shortcuts will create results that cannot be cleanly reused or audited later.
hidden_assumptions: When the project refers to "the Airbnb data," it means the cleaned feature-store mirror of the Airbnb booking task that the lab currently treats as its canonical internal copy.

To "replicate the paper first" means reproducing the headline task and broad comparison using the lab's current default preprocessing and training harness rather than reconstructing old bespoke steps.
The "standard split" is whatever the current pipeline auto-generates for this benchmark, namely the lab's default 80/10/10 split on the current snapshot.
Results are not really "draft-ready" until the main runs are complete across the usual seed count, the artifacts are logged, and the tables can be reproduced directly from tracked configs.

misalignment_points.topic: Which Airbnb dataset is being used
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both casually refer to "the Airbnb data" as if it were a single obvious dataset.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the archived Kaggle New User Bookings snapshot used in earlier reproductions, with its original row set and raw feature layout.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the lab's cleaned internal mirror of the Airbnb booking task, which has duplicate handling and a few standardized preprocessing adjustments baked in.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both versions are locally known by the same shorthand, have nearly identical column names, and are seen as interchangeable lab assets, so the phrase feels too routine to trigger clarification.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to replicate first
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to "replicate the paper first" before adding extensions.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means staying close to the original setup in spirit and implementation boundaries, including legacy preprocessing conventions and evaluation structure, so the comparison is faithful before any modernization.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means reproducing the same prediction task and headline comparisons while naturally using the lab's current training pipeline, preprocessing defaults, and tracking stack.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In research meetings, "replicate first" often sounds unambiguous because both people think it simply means being conservative, but one hears fidelity to the original workflow while the other hears fidelity to the problem statement.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the standard split
misalignment_points.surface_form: They mention using "the standard split" without elaboration.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 presupposes there is an already-established fixed split file for this exact task from the old reproduction repo and assumes Kai will use that.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 presupposes there is no special historical split worth reviving and assumes "standard" means the current pipeline's default split generation on the present data snapshot.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both treat the split as settled background infrastructure rather than a live design choice, so neither expects it to require discussion in a planning meeting.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They set a milestone for "draft-ready results" by next Wednesday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks this means enough evidence to begin writing: one comparison table, a few stable runs, and uncertainty summaries sufficient for the argument.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks this means the experiments meet the lab's reproducibility threshold: full seed coverage, logged artifacts, and tables generated from tracked runs.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds like ordinary project-management shorthand, and each person's criterion is professionally reasonable, so the surface agreement feels complete even though their completeness standards differ.
